title: 600-Series Feasibility Analysis

proposal.purpose: Dedicated operational lane for content authoring, distractor engineering, and EC expansion
proposal.status: Pure proposal — no files, sessions, or artifacts exist

analysis.expectedThroughputGain: 15-20% improvement in authoring velocity (items/session) through dedicated tools/infrastructure
analysis.startupCost: 3-4 sessions to build 600-series infrastructure (authoring tools, quality gates, template systems)
analysis.breakeven: Session 7+ — startup investment equals savings by session 7-8
analysis.netImpact: NEUTRAL to SLIGHTLY POSITIVE (0-1 session net saving)

whyDefer: Startup cost (3-4 sessions) nearly equals projected savings (3-4 sessions) — near-zero net benefit
800-series certification methodology already embeds EW authoring — 600-series would add a handoff layer, not eliminate one
The binding constraint is AUTHOR CAPACITY (human time to write explanations), not infrastructure. Tools can't write explanations — they can only accelerate review of what's written
Domain E/F certification (316 items) would need to wait for 600-series infrastructure to be built before receiving benefit — delaying the critical path
Portfolio already has a proven toolchain: governance guard, validation scripts, parse checks. A new lane adds governance overhead without proportional throughput gain
whatWouldJustify600series: If EW authoring velocity were observed to be the binding constraint and tooling could demonstrably accelerate it by >40%
If we discovered systematic distractor quality issues requiring specialized analysis tools that don't exist
If content operations volume were 3x current (e.g., 5,000+ items needing full EC/EW)
recommendation: DEFER. Re-evaluate after 800-series Waves 2-3 if authoring velocity proves to be the actual bottleneck. The current constraint analysis (Agents E/F) shows the bottleneck is item readiness (archived clones, greenfield authoring), not tooling inadequacy.
